Glossary

Robots.txt: what is this file for search engines?

robots.txt is a text file placed at the root of a website, telling search engine bots which parts they may visit and which to leave alone. It is a sign at the entrance, not a lock.

The definition in one sentence

Google, Bing and other services send out bots, programs that browse websites to read them. Before going in, a polite bot first looks at the robots.txt file, at the address yourwebsite.fr/robots.txt. There it finds simple instructions, such as “do not go into this folder”.

The file can also say where the sitemap is, the list of pages to discover.

What it does for a small business

On a small website, robots.txt is mostly used to stop bots wasting their time in areas of no interest: the admin, internal search pages, shopping baskets, technical files. That way, bots focus on your real pages.

A real-life example

While a website is being built, the provider adds a line that forbids bots from everything, so the work in progress stays out of sight. The website goes live, but nobody removes the line. Months later, the manager wonders why they never show up in Google. One forgotten line was blocking everything.

What you need to know

  • It is not a protection. The file is public, anyone can read it, and malicious bots ignore it. A secret page must be protected by a password.
  • Blocking a page does not remove it from Google. A blocked address can still appear if other websites link to it. To make it disappear, you need a “noindex” instruction on the page itself.
  • A small mistake can have big effects. One slash too many, and the whole website is closed to bots.
  • Do not block the style files, or Google will see your website as a page with no formatting.

If your website still does not appear in Google at all after several weeks, robots.txt is one of the first things to check.

Your questions

Does my website need a robots.txt file?

It is not compulsory: without one, bots assume they can visit everything. Having a well-configured one lets you point to the sitemap and keep bots away from useless areas.

Can you block the bots of artificial intelligence tools?

Some of these bots follow the instructions given in robots.txt, others do not. It is a choice to make depending on your business, bearing in mind that the file remains a request and not a barrier.
